edges.description: Effector cytokines from activated T cells drive keratinocyte proliferation and plaque formation.
Dendritic-cell-derived IL-23 initiates the central psoriatic cytokine circuit.
IL-23 expands IL-17-producing T-cell responses that sustain plaque inflammation.
IL-36-driven neutrophilic inflammation produces sterile pustules.

Exogenous IL-17A/IL-22 reproduces the downstream IL-17/IL-22 effector output of the axis, namely keratinocyte-driven inflammatory mediator secretion and a psoriasis-like hallmark transcriptional signature (TNF-alpha/NF-kB, IL6/JAK/STAT3), together with its JAK-dependent pharmacologic reversibility.
edges.limitations: Cytokines are applied exogenously to healthy-donor skin, so the model does not reproduce IL-23-driven Th17 differentiation, dendritic-cell or T-cell activation, or a psoriatic genetic background; only tissue-resident immune cells are present, with no recruitment of circulating immune cells.
edges.source: Outer Biosciences long-term ex vivo human skin platform

edges.description: IL-17A/IL-22 stimulation reproduces the psoriasiform keratinocyte-remodeling program of this node: suppression of terminal barrier and differentiation genes (FLG, FLG2, LORICRIN, DSC1) with psoriasiform histopathology (dyskeratosis, parakeratosis, subcorneal separation) over three weeks. In psoriatic epidermis the hyperproliferative and impaired-differentiation arms are coupled faces of this regenerative program.
edges.limitations: The dataset evidences the impaired-differentiation and psoriasiform histopathology arm; the keratinocyte proliferation rate itself was not separately quantified, and the tissue lacks a psoriatic genetic background.
edges.source: Outer Biosciences long-term ex vivo human skin platform

edges.description: Concurrent tofacitinib (JAK inhibitor) reverses the IL-17/IL-22-induced inflammatory transcriptional program, mediator secretion, and barrier-gene repression, and attenuates the psoriasiform histopathology, demonstrating that the induced state is pharmacologically reversible and that immune signaling remains responsive over weeks of culture.
edges.limitations: Attenuation of secreted IL-8 was more modest than of MCP-1, S100A8/9, and MMP1, consistent with partial persistence of JAK-independent inflammatory signaling.
edges.source: Outer Biosciences long-term ex vivo human skin platform

nodes.description: A long-term ex vivo human skin platform in which native full-thickness biopsies are maintained at an air-liquid interface for up to four weeks with preserved epidermal, stromal, and tissue-resident immune programs. Sustained basal-media IL-17A/IL-22 stimulation drives a psoriasiform inflammatory program (induction of IL36A, DEFB4A/B, S100A12, CXCL1/CXCL8, IL6, and MMP1 with suppression of epidermal barrier and differentiation genes such as FLG, FLG2, LORICRIN, and DSC1) that is broadly reversed by the JAK inhibitor tofacitinib, providing a human-tissue model of the IL-17/IL-22 effector arm of psoriasis and its pharmacologic modulation.
